annotationRationale: All routes split the quadrilateral along AC and determine the missing height of triangle ABC. Similarity, coordinate equations, and chord products provide distinct ways to find that height; their concepts remain attached to the individual methods.

review.questionCheck: Independently, placing A=(0,0), C=(20,0), D=(20,30) gives BD: y=2(x-5). The right-angle condition yields B=(2,-6) or (10,10); only the first puts E on segment BD. The area is 300+60=360, choice D. The segment-intersection condition resolves the configuration without a figure; no contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Similarity, coordinate equations and intersecting chords provide three distinct accessible routes. Further supplied routes are redundant, substantially longer or use excluded trigonometry.
review.annotationCheck: Composite area is the common assessed outcome, with triangle area supporting it. The central height-finding concepts are recorded precisely on the individual routes, so the question-level area tag does not replace them.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The projection order A,F,E,C is valid. Similarity gives BF=2x, and the justified altitude relation gives 4x²=(5-x)(15+x). Its roots are 3 and -5; x=3 also satisfies x<5, so BF=6 and the area is 360.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The argument accurately follows AoPS Solution 1 while adding independent configuration and altitude-relation explanations. It is correctly labeled third-party-informed original work.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The missing height motivates the construction. The similarity correspondences, unfamiliar altitude identity, root selection and area addition are sufficiently explained without another diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All four IDs are used directly: similarity criteria, proportional corresponding sides, solving a quadratic by factoring and composite area.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The line equation and squared-distance equation are correct. Substitution produces 5(x-2)(x-10)=0. The segment condition requires x<5 and y<0, selecting B=(2,-6), hence area 360.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The coordinate setup matches LIVE and AoPS Solution 2. Expressing the right angle through Pythagorean distances is an independent elementary reconstruction; it does not inherit the vector terminology and sign errors in AoPS Solution 6.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The axes are motivated by the perpendicular known sides. Both equations and the decisive rejection of the second intersection are explained.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Slope computation, point-slope form, Pythagorean distances, quadratic factoring and area decomposition each justify their attached ID.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Similarity gives OG=10, placing G on the diameter circle. EG=5√5 and intersecting chords give EB=75/(5√5)=3√5. The final similar triangles give BH=10·3/5=6, so the area is 360.

methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why the auxiliary circle point is useful. The diameter property, chord-product rule and final height proportion are stated sufficiently for an AMC 10 learner to follow.

review.mathCheck: The projection order A,F,E,C is valid. Similarity gives BF=2x, and the justified altitude relation gives 4x²=(5-x)(15+x). Its roots are 3 and -5; x=3 also satisfies x<5, so BF=6 and the area is 360. The line equation and squared-distance equation are correct. Substitution produces 5(x-2)(x-10)=0. The segment condition requires x<5 and y<0, selecting B=(2,-6), hence area 360. Similarity gives OG=10, placing G on the diameter circle. EG=5√5 and intersecting chords give EB=75/(5√5)=3√5. The final similar triangles give BH=10·3/5=6, so the area is 360.
review.sourceMethodCheck: The argument accurately follows AoPS Solution 1 while adding independent configuration and altitude-relation explanations. Expressing the right angle through Pythagorean distances is an independent elementary reconstruction; it does not inherit the vector terminology and sign errors in AoPS Solution 6. This accurately reconstructs AoPS Solution 7 with original explanatory prose and explicit identification of the circle and chord segments. The nonofficial source-informed-original designation is correct.
